data_model.signal: 5 related custom objects, Master-Detail on Match_Assignment, two Team lookups on Match (Home/Away) — standard 3-5 object relational model

automation.signal: Validation rule (block edits on Set match) + duplicate rule (Match + Staff Member unique) — declarative, low DML, no Apex

ui.signal: Standard Lightning page layouts for Admin persona; no LWC required

size_rationale: M — driven by 5-object relational model with junction relationship; automation and UI are lightweight declarative config
complexity_drivers: Five net-new custom objects with relational dependencies (M-D, dual lookups). Validation rule and duplicate rule are the only automation. Admin works entirely in standard UI.
risks: Field-level validation rules not fully specified — assumed standard; confirm Admin UX requirements before field schema is finalised.
solution_approach: Custom object build via Setup UI or SFDX metadata. Standard page layouts. Validation rule on Match_Assignment (Status = Set blocks edits). Duplicate rule on (Match__c, Staff_Member__c).

intelligence_ai.signal: 5 custom Agentforce Actions, custom Topic with instruction engineering, confirmation-gate design, scope-limiting guardrails, agent persona tuning — multi-action agent requiring iterative prompt/instruction work [extends: agent-customization-with-apex Trailhead trail]

automation.signal: Permission set creation + agent surface configuration — declarative setup

size_rationale: L — driven by multi-action agent complexity: 5 custom actions, instruction engineering, confirmation gate, and scope guardrails require iteration and testing to get natural-language mapping reliable
complexity_drivers: Agentforce agent configuration is the UX layer for this build. Getting the natural-language → action mapping reliable across 5 actions, with a confirmation gate and scope-limiting instructions, takes careful instruction design and iterative testing. Not a simple plug-and-play configuration.
skills_needed: Agentforce specialist (topic/action/instruction design), Salesforce Developer (Apex invocable wiring), QA (conversation testing)
risks: Agent instruction quality determines demo reliability. Poor guardrails will cause the agent to attempt out-of-scope actions or skip the confirmation gate. Instruction testing with realistic Organiser prompts is required before demo day.
solution_approach: One Topic (Match_Operations), 5 Actions each backed by an Apex @InvocableMethod. Agent instructions engineered to: (1) always confirm before assigning, (2) decline out-of-scope requests, (3) surface conflict errors clearly. Permission set Match_Organiser assigned to demo user.

automation.signal: 3 Apex @InvocableMethod classes with custom datetime overlap SOQL, multi-condition business rule enforcement (crew minimums per role, role uniqueness, stadium conflict), inline re-validation in StaffAssigner, status lifecycle management — multiple DML paths and branching logic [assumption: standard Agentforce Apex invocable pattern; validated by Trailhead agent-customization-with-apex]

data_model.signal: Read-only queries against existing objects; no new schema

size_rationale: L — driven by Apex complexity: custom datetime overlap detection (touching-times boundary condition), 3 invocable classes with branching logic, inline re-validation, minimum-threshold checking. One dominant driver; no breadth bump needed.
complexity_drivers: The overlap detection SOQL is the hardest piece: must correctly handle the touching-times boundary (start B <= end A). Three separate Apex classes each with distinct logic: (1) availability checker + stadium conflict, (2) assigner with re-validation + status update, (3) confirmer with threshold check + Set transition. Non-trivial Apex test data setup required to cover all conflict scenarios.
risks: Overlap detection bug silently breaks the demo. Test coverage must include: (a) touching times, (b) fully overlapping matches, (c) no-conflict case, (d) partial crew assignment across sessions. Governor limits are not a concern at demo scale (5 matches, 18 staff) but note for Phase 2 scaling.
solution_approach: Three @InvocableMethod Apex classes: StaffAvailabilityChecker (datetime SOQL overlap check + stadium conflict), StaffAssigner (re-validate + insert Match_Assignment + status update to Staffing), MatchConfirmer (threshold check + update status to Set + return crew summary). Hardcoded thresholds as final static integers. Apex test classes with realistic conflict scenarios.
solution_approach_notes: size_if_assumption_breaks: L is solid regardless; if Phase 2 requires configurable thresholds (Custom Metadata + admin UI), add S to the estimate at that point

automation.signal: SFDX metadata deploy + anonymous Apex reset script (delete assignments, reset statuses) — scripted, low logic complexity

data_model.signal: Seed data insertion only; no schema changes

size_rationale: S — deployment pipeline + seed data + reset script; main risk is operational (deployment sequence), not technical complexity
complexity_drivers: Straightforward SFDX deploy + data seeding. Reset script is 5 lines of anonymous Apex. Seed data must be designed deliberately: Match 3 pre-seeded with 2 Camera Operators to create visible conflicts; at least 1 staff per role with a time-overlapping assignment on another match.
skills_needed: Salesforce Developer (SFDX deployment), Demo owner (script rehearsal and reset procedure)
risks: Deployment sequence matters — objects must deploy before agent config, agent config before seed data. Post-deploy smoke test required. Demo owner must know the reset procedure and run it before each session.
solution_approach: sf project deploy start from SFDX project. Anonymous Apex seed data script (or Data Loader CSV import). Anonymous Apex reset script: delete all Match_Assignment__c, reset all Match Status__c to Draft. Post-deploy verification: confirm agent is active in Agent Studio, run demo flow once end-to-end.
